labeling_rule: Same fact: both records state the same proposition about the same subject: one event or occurrence, state, attribute, relationship, preference or plan. Wording, word order, a name in place of I, hedges and filler do not matter, and neither does the date a line shows when both dates refer to the same occurrence or state. A record that says everything the other says and adds detail is still the same fact, because the other line adds nothing beside it. Where a line leaves a reference open (it, that, there), the claim's subject, predicate and object and its source turn decide what it refers to. Different facts: each record states something the other does not: another event, or the same kind of event on another occasion; another object, attribute, person, place, amount, time or polarity; or a detail on each side that the other lacks. A different-fact pair is also marked with the one thing that alone separates it, if there is one: number (the same proposition with another count or amount), date (the same kind of event or statement on another date or occasion) or negation (one record denies what the other asserts).
